name: Ghanaian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only a dictionary (Deutsch & McGuire) and survey notes; sign language, no stress description located.

sources.citation: Antwi, Mike Ofori. 2024. Information Structure in Ghanaian Sign Language. MPhil thesis, University of Ghana, Legon (UGSpace handle 123456789/45200).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 1.3.1.1 'Phonetics and phonology' (pp. 6-10) describes GhSL phonology as handshape, location, movement, orientation and non-manual markers ('sometimes called visual prosody'); nothing on word stress. Ch. 3-4 treat sentence-level prosodic marking of focus/topic (raised eyebrows 'reb', holds, pauses; sentence-final position prominent) -- phrase-level information-structure prosody, not word stress. The only 'stress shifting' passage (p. 44) is about spoken languages in the literature review.

sources.citation: Edward, Mary & George Akanlig-Pare. 2021. Sign language research in Ghana: An overview of indigenous and foreign-based sign languages. Journal of African Languages and Literatures 2: 114-137.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey; p. 124 summarises GSL phonology work (Edward 2014; Akanlig-Pare 2013, 2014) as covering 'Articulatory Parameters (Handshape, Orientation, Location and Movement), Nonmanual markers, Minimal pairs and Free variation'; no mention of stress or word-level prominence.

sources.citation: Edward, Mary. 2020. Lexical iconicity in Adamorobe Sign Language (AdaSL) and Ghanaian Sign Language (GSL). In N. Pawlak & I. Will (eds.), West African languages: Linguistic theory and communication, 230-251. Warsaw: WUW. doi 10.31338/uw.9788323546313
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 233 fn. 6: 'The phonology is primarily made up of the articulatory parameters and the non-manual makers.. The non-manual markers in sign languages rely on facial expression and the position of the body and these act as prosodic cues to the sign.' General sign-phonology remark; no word-stress statement.
